title: Cordex

seo.title: Cordex Industrial Landing Page Design & Prompt | Ottermind
seo.description: Landing page reference for an industrial company — a stats row, #0A0A0B base, one self-contained HTML file and 0.7s transitions. Copy the prompt or open it staged in Studio.

tagline: “We protect transport safer across all industries” — the whole landing page is composed around that line, down to the animation timings.
summary: Landing page reference for an industrial company — a stats row, #0A0A0B base, one self-contained HTML file and 0.7s transitions.
about: Read Cordex as a landing page spec: the values were written down before the page was built. It leads with “We protect transport safer across all industries” and gives that line the frame rather than shrinking it into a card. Colour is limited to black #0A0A0B underneath, #F7F7F8 for the type and red #E23B32 carrying the accents, set in Inter. Delivery is one self-contained HTML file, captured at 1920x1416 so the frame is fixed before any code is written. The motion budget is 0.7s transitions and a looping video bed. It is most useful when the Industrial landing page has to survive a copy change without a redesign.

layout.title: The bar shares the page grid
layout.body: Links sit on one line at a single size, and the #E23B32 action closes the row on the right so the eye finishes where the navigation ends. Labels are short enough to fit one line at 480px, and the active item is marked with weight rather than with a pill. One action per bar.

layout.title: A full-bleed clip behind the type
layout.body: A 6.8s clip at 1920x1416 does the atmospheric work; the brief fixes its crop and leaves the type untouched on top of it. Export at 1920x1416 or wider and the cover crop keeps working.

layout.title: The grid sets the order
layout.body: The grid does the reading order for you: panels of equal weight, one idea each, set in Inter at a small size so the structure stays visible. Panel heights are driven by the copy, so a longer line does not break the alignment of the row. Keep one idea per panel.

layout.title: Fluid where it needs to be
layout.body: The brief uses a clamp between 12px and 21px for the headline, which is what keeps a long line from breaking awkwardly. Because the scale is clamped, the display line never jumps between breakpoints.

motion.title: Ambient motion without a scroll library
motion.body: Ambient movement comes from the 6.8s 1920x1416 loop rather than from scroll effects, which keeps the page calm and the type readable. The loop is cropped to cover, which means the composition does not depend on a particular frame size.

motion.title: State changes, timed
motion.body: The controls resolve in 0.7s, fast enough that the page answers as it is touched rather than after it. Easing is specified alongside the duration (0.7s), so a rebuild cannot quietly substitute a different feel.

style.glass: Panels are translucent over black #0A0A0B, and the type on top stays at full contrast so the effect never costs readability.

fonts.name: Inter
fonts.role: Headline and interface text — one face for the whole page

editorial.title: The order behind the landing page
editorial.body: Attention is routed rather than scattered. “We protect transport safer across all industries” is doing that work from the first frame. The eye lands on the display line first, then the supporting copy, then the action. Proof, where it appears, stays a strip or a row rather than a wall of testimonials. That sequence is the design. A industrial reader gets the offer before the options.

editorial.title: The numbers behind the landing page
editorial.body: The brief is a specification, not a mood board. It fixes type from 12px to 21px, 100vh sections, 14px spacing steps, 0.7s transitions and a 480px breakpoint, and it names the media at 1920x1416 and a 6.8s loop. That level of detail is why the design survives a rebuild: change the copy and the relationships still hold. Nothing in this landing page depends on a default.

editorial.title: How the landing page reflows
editorial.body: A designed narrow layout takes more decisions than a squeeze. The brief pays for them: the type is clamped between 12px and 21px, the layout shifts at 480px and the section is held at 100vh, stated rather than discovered at build time. The narrow layout is a decision rather than a squeeze, and the hierarchy survives it.

faq.question: Why does the entry name one self-contained HTML file at all?
faq.answer: Cordex was built in one self-contained HTML file, and the entry says so for provenance. The brief describes positions, sizes and timings, so it rebuilds in any framework that can set type and place elements.

faq.question: Why is Cordex's prompt not printed here?
faq.answer: Everything quoted on the page comes from the captured 29,696-character brief rather than from a description written afterwards. That is why the numbers and the prose agree.

faq.question: Is the Cordex prompt a finished spec or a starting point?
faq.answer: It is a build brief rather than a mood description: it names the composition at 1920x1416, the spacing and the motion values. Nothing in it treats the rendered image as the source of truth.
